content.text:
Here's what's on each dashboard today, so my suggestions build on reality:

- **Retail** (`dashboard.tsx`): circle graph + today / 7-day / 30-day completed counts, active (pending) count. Chart-led.
- **Property** (`property-dashboard.tsx`): 4-stat strip (tenants · outstanding · queued · paused) + "rent transactions" list. *"Collected this month" is computed but not surfaced.*
- **Trades** (`trades-dashboard.tsx`): near-identical mirror — (clients · outstanding · queued · paused) + "job invoices" list. Same buried "collected this month".

One pattern jumps out: **all three lead with counts, but the number a business owner actually opens the app to see is money** — takings/collection. That's my biggest single recommendation across the board.

## Guiding budget (so it never gets crowded)
Each mobile dashboard gets **one hero + a 3–4 stat strip + one action-forward list + one forward-looking widget.** Anything richer (trends, breakdowns, history) lives in **Analytics**, not the dashboard. I've tagged each item **[core]** (on the dashboard) or **[premium]** (paid-tier unlock) and called out what to deliberately *leave off*.

---

## Retail
**Hero:** Today's takings $ (with ▲/▼ vs same weekday last week) **[core]**
**Stat strip (4):** transactions today · avg sale · pending/unsettled · refunds today **[core]**
**Action list:** recent transactions (live, SSE) — you have this **[core]**
**Forward widget:** next payout/settlement — amount + date **[core]** — merchants constantly ask "when do I get paid?"

**Premium:**
- **Peak hours / busiest day** heatmap strip — staffing & promo insight **[premium]**
- **Repeat-customer rate** — % returning vs new (needs payer fingerprint) **[premium]**
- **Goal tracker** — set a daily/weekly takings target, ring fills through the day **[premium]**
- Leave off the dashboard: full revenue charts, product/category breakdown → Analytics.

## Property
**Hero:** Collection this month — **collected $ / expected $** as a progress ring (the one number that matters) **[core]**
**Stat strip (4):** active tenants · **arrears $** (not just count) · due in next 7 days · failed/paused schedules **[core]**
**Action list:** rent transactions with status — you have this; add a **"needs attention"** filter (overdue + failed) pinned to top **[core]**
**Forward widget:** **expected cash, next 30 days** from recurring schedules — simple forecast **[core]**

**Premium:**
- **Arrears aging** (0–7 / 8–30 / 30+ days) with one-tap **chase/reminder** **[premium]** — this is the killer property feature
- **Tenant reliability score** — on-time payment history per tenant **[premium]**
- **Auto-chase status** — "3 reminders sent, 1 promise-to-pay" **[premium]**
- **Occupancy / units summary** if you model properties **[premium]**
- Leave off: per-property P&L, full ledger → Analytics.

## Trades
**Hero:** **Outstanding $ owed to you** (across deposits + balances) — tradies live and die by cashflow **[core]**
**Stat strip (4):** open quotes (count + **$ value**) · jobs in progress · due this week · collected this month **[core]**
**Action list:** job invoices — you have this; reframe as **"jobs needing action"**: *accept-pending quotes, deposit-paid → send balance, balance-paid → mark complete* (drives the lifecycle) **[core]**
**Forward widget:** **pipeline** — value of quotes awaiting acceptance + this week's scheduled/recurring work **[core]**

**Premium:**
- **Quote conversion rate** + **avg days-to-accept** — turns quoting into a measurable funnel **[premium]**
- **Deposit conversion** — % accepted quotes that paid deposit **[premium]**
- **Avg days-to-pay** per client + slow-payer flag **[premium]**
- **Job profitability** (quote total − materials, if you capture line-item costs) **[premium]**
- Leave off: full revenue/GST history → Analytics (already exists).

---

## Cross-cutting premium layer (applies to all three, builds the "premium product" feel)
- **Tap any stat → drill into Analytics** (dashboard stays clean, depth is one tap away)
- **Smart insights card** — one rotating, plain-English nudge: *"Takings down 12% vs last Tue"* / *"$2,400 in arrears 30+ days"* / *"4 quotes worth $9k awaiting reply"*
- **Customisable hero** — let the merchant pick which metric is the hero
- **Notifications/digest** — daily or weekly summary (push/email): the dashboard, delivered
- **CSV / accounting export** (Xero/MYOB for NZ) — premium gate
- **Multi-user / staff roles** — classic premium upsell

---

My honest take on priorities if you want the highest impact for least crowding: **(1)** make the hero a money number on all three, **(2)** add the forward-looking widget (payout / expected cash / pipeline) — it's what turns a "log" into a "dashboard," and **(3)** the rotating smart-insight card is the cheapest thing that makes it *feel* premium.

Want me to take one vertical (I'd start with Trades or Property since they share structure) and turn the **[core]** set into a concrete spec + implementation plan? Or adjust the list first — e.g. if you model data I'm assuming you don't (units/occupancy, line-item material costs), tell me and I'll re-tune.

Audit complete. I changed **nothing** — this is identification only, and every item below was independently verified (hard grep for static + dynamic/lazy imports across `client/src`, `server`, `shared`), not just taken from the tool. I've split findings by confidence so you can act safely.

A quick note on method: I confirmed the live stack is **Windcave** (payments), **JWT** (`server/auth.ts`, auth), and **Resend** (email) — which is what makes the Stripe/passport/SendGrid packages genuinely dead rather than dynamically-used. I also caught one tool false-positive (knip claims `landing-page.tsx`'s export is unused — it's your live PR #2 landing page), which is why I'm flagging the "exports" category as unreliable.

---

## TIER 1 — Dead files, fully verified (0 importers anywhere) ✅ safe

**Old landing-page cluster** (superseded by your current `landing-page.tsx`; these form one self-contained orphaned island — none imported by anything live):
- `components/CustomerExperienceSection.tsx`, `FeaturesSection.tsx`, `FinalCTASection.tsx`, `HowItWorksSection.tsx`, `PricingSection.tsx`, `TerminalFeaturesSection.tsx`
- `components/ImageWithFallback.tsx` (only used *by* `FeaturesSection`, which is itself dead)
- `components/navigation.tsx`, `mobile-header.tsx`, `layout.tsx`

**Orphaned payment UI** (not wired into checkout/terminal — possibly planned Apple/Google Pay that never landed):
- `components/digital-wallet-buttons.tsx`, `native-payment-buttons.tsx`, `mobile-payment-interface.tsx`

**Orphaned admin** (App.tsx uses an *inline* `AdminProtectedRoute` + lazy-loads `AdminDashboard`, leaving these older standalones dead):
- `pages/admin/ProtectedAdminRoute.tsx`, `pages/admin/WebsiteAnalytics.tsx`

**Orphaned hook / lib / middleware:**
- `hooks/use-scramble-text.ts`, `lib/themes.ts`, `server/middleware/merchant-validation.ts`

→ **18 files**, all confirmed zero-importer.

## TIER 2 — Unused UI-kit primitives (shadcn) ✅ safe, but conventionally kept

26 unused `components/ui/*`: `accordion, aspect-ratio, avatar, breadcrumb, calendar, carousel, chart, collapsible, command, context-menu, drawer, dropdown-menu, hover-card, input-otp, menubar, navigation-menu, pagination, popover, radio-group, resizable, scroll-area, sidebar, skeleton, slider, toggle-group, toggle`.

These are a vendored component library — safe to delete, but many teams keep the full kit so primitives are on hand. **My recommendation: leave these.** Low clutter cost, and you'll likely reach for some as you build the dashboard features.

## TIER 3 — Unused dependencies (verified) ✅ safe to uninstall
- **Legacy auth** (you use JWT): `passport`, `passport-local`, `passport-google-oauth20`, `openid-client`, `express-session`, `connect-pg-simple`, `memorystore` (+ their `@types/*`)
- **Legacy payments** (you use Windcave): `stripe`, `stripe-replit-sync`, `@stripe/react-stripe-js`, `@stripe/stripe-js`
- **Legacy email** (you use Resend): `@sendgrid/mail`
- **Backing the unused UI kit**: ~17 `@radix-ui/react-*`, `cmdk`, `vaul`, `embla-carousel-react`, `react-day-picker`, `input-otp`, `react-resizable-panels`, `next-themes` — *only remove these if you also remove Tier 2*
- **Other**: `react-icons`, `memoizee`, `topojson-client`, `@capacitor/ios`, `playwright` (dev), `prettier`/`eslint-plugin-prettier` (only if you don't lint), `tw-animate-css`, `zod-validation-error`, `@jridgewell/trace-mapping`
- ⚠️ Note: the `stripe_*` **DB columns** in `schema.ts` are separate — leave the schema alone; only the npm package is dead.

## TIER 4 — Unused exports ⚠️ low confidence, do NOT bulk-remove
Knip lists 54, but it false-flagged the live landing page, so this list needs per-symbol verification. Mostly harmless re-exports inside the UI kit. A few *might* be real (e.g. `useNotifications`, `decodeJWT`/`getCurrentUser` in `lib/auth.ts`, `clearAllUsers` in `server/auth.ts`) — but each needs hand-checking. I'd skip this category unless you want me to verify specific ones.

## Bonus finding (the opposite problem)
`nanoid` is **used** in `server/vite.ts` but **not declared** in `package.json` (it resolves transitively). Worth adding explicitly so a dependency bump doesn't break the build.
